claims.claim: Reviewers find naval battles to be confusing.

citations.review_text: great game lots of community support great tutorials only bad part is confusing naval battles

I'd say this is one of the more polished Total War games, it mixes the fun of melee-styled Total War, including the Rise of the Samurai DLC building around this further. SHOGUN 2 has a mix of stuff similar to Total War Empire and Napoleon with the Fall of the Samurai DLC, introducing firearms and more modern equipment. Honestly, I really like the game taking place in the Shogunate and Imperial era of Japan as it feels like a really cool scenario and quite a niche time in history that not many people look at.

Combat is quite smooth and fun, and I find that the campaigns in SHOGUN 2 play very interestingly and in my opinion are very fun compared to a lot of other Total War games.

Naval combat is done quite well in SHOGUN 2 compared to previous titles.

I don't have too much to say mainly cause I haven't played it for that long but it is quite a fun game and I reccomend it to anyone who enjoys the Total War series or tactical styled top down games in general.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that diplomacy is very limited and functions more like a mere suggestion during campaigns.

citations.review_text: Fairly new to the Total War scene, so from a newbies perspective this is a really good one. I've played a tiny bit of Rome 2, and some Napoleon. But this is by far better than those. With very few mods you can have a great time. It can be very rough however, even on the lowest difficulties you can be punished a lot, which can be a plus for those who like a challenge, but understand the game has one issue, that is that the AI does not play by game rules, diplomacy is very minimal, and often it may feel like the AI is pulling things out of their ass when they should be broke beyond comprehension. Otherwise good game there's not a lot else to say, I have had some crashes here and there but if you save often it shouldn't be a huge deal.
holy moly. This game is sooo good. But diplomacy is a mere suggestion in this game. AI is also relentless so get ready for total war

claims.claim: Reviewers state that settlements display wealth rather than factual income, making actual earnings harder to determine.

citations.review_text:
Its probably more a me thing but i didn't like this too much. Compared to other Total war you don't get any post battle loot/prisoners meaning one good source of income is just gone from this edition if you get zerged by ai on higher levels you just have to deal with it.

Most come from the economy in this game. 

The base Yari is so strong that they can carry you through the entire campaign on medium difficulty. 

The settlements don't display their factual income bothers me a lot too, they show 'wealth' which you tax so they display 1000+ but you may only get 20% of that making it 200 so you can own a goldmine and still feel dirt poor. 

Units cost their full upkeep even when damaged, tho some other titles do this too just means that even tho this have a replenish system unlike Medieval II you kind of want to combine very hurt units rather than replenish them to get rid of their upkeep even if hiring new ones also cost money. 

The General units feel weird, they are super weak in this mostly due to a many early units are spears which just melts cav in this. Sure cav was a little too good in Medieval II. 

The Free estate design of Cities is a bit weird too, you get very few defenders in the base game, semed to be a bit better in the expansion but base you just get one or two defenders at early city levels. In like Med II you had to recruit militias yourself that was free in cities sure but... 

The Forts are also really tiny, still worth holding them but archers can reach most of the fort just standing outside even if higher levels make it a bit better.

5/10:  This game is a beta release that never got finished.  There are no cities or even towns; just a fort on top of a dirt mound.  The towers are pathetic, special abilities are a joke, like fire arrows that last for a single shot before they run out, meaning towers often won't catch fire and it takes literally five (5) minutes for the ability to be reset.  Because...   The enemy agents are brutal, even in Easy Mode, "cities" will randomly have Unrest for no reason, and you never have enough resources or time to do anything you want, like taking the capital, Kyoto.  Mount Fuji looks like it was made with Microsoft Paint in battles.  

You either have to commit to a strong army, a strong navy, major income buildings, or agent buildings.  That's it.  You would think you could spread the love around, but no.  If you do that, you hurt yourself and everything but what you focus on is mediocre at best, because each piece of this game is vital to your survival.  Therefore, it's nearly impossible to win the game given the specific win conditions it gives you.  

The starting units are absolutely worthess, which means you have to wait and upgrade your army with samurai before you can even start conquering.  Japan feels exceptionally small, the quests are extremely basic, and very little is explained.  And when it is, it is explained slowly with a heavy Japanese accent.  For authenticity, of course...  

You can't even invade China or Korea, despite the fact that in historical reality, Toyotomi Hideoshi sent 300,000 samurai to Korea during this time period to mess up stuff on the continent.  Also, there was no Shogun (with power) until Togugawa Ieyasu took over after the civil wars were nearly at an end.  There was the Emperor in Kyoto, but he had very little power and no army to mess up your conquest...

The battles are "kind-of" fun?  Smoother unit movement than most other games, less friendly fire, chasing down fleeing units is easier, and the blood graphics are …

citations.review_text: Fairly new to the Total War scene, so from a newbies perspective this is a really good one. I've played a tiny bit of Rome 2, and some Napoleon. But this is by far better than those. With very few mods you can have a great time. It can be very rough however, even on the lowest difficulties you can be punished a lot, which can be a plus for those who like a challenge, but understand the game has one issue, that is that the AI does not play by game rules, diplomacy is very minimal, and often it may feel like the AI is pulling things out of their ass when they should be broke beyond comprehension. Otherwise good game there's not a lot else to say, I have had some crashes here and there but if you save often it shouldn't be a huge deal.

I really like the game but I have one complaint, the modding experience genuinely sucks.

The mod manager barely explains load order, conflicts, dependencies, or why a mod is marked as outdated. You add one or two mods, launch the game through five different menus, select DirectX 11, and then the game immediately closes with no error message.

Was it the new mod? The load order? A conflict? An outdated mod? Who knows. Sometimes removing the mods you just added does not even fix it, because the old working load order has somehow broken too. there is no save load order. if you want to save a order take picture or video. trouble shooting? just take note and reopen the game again n again and pray.

The game might have a 35-40 mods limit. I cannot confirm but from testing if you pass that limit the game will crash no matter if you use trash or perfect load order. trash load order 39 mod work. perfect load order 41 mod crash

Seriously F this game. Terrible optimization, they removed multiplayer and added their spyware launcher and while you think you are doing well and are having fun, the AI starts acting stupid or is blatantly cheating.
Co-op crashing simulator. if you like restarting the game every 15 minutes please do buy.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that diplomacy can be unpredictable and unreliable, with certain factions refusing to deal with the player despite friendly standing.

citations.review_text:
Shogun 2 although released over a decade ago is arguably the best game in the Total War series. While later entries introduced larger campaigns, more factions, or even the non historical counter part such as the Warhammer series, none have matched Shogun 2's near perfect balance of strategic depth, tactical combat, and focused design.

Although not as indepth as later entries such as Three Kingdoms or even older one's such as Napoleon, the economy and diplomacy are remarkably wellbalanced. Province management is straightforward, focusing on taxation, agriculture, trade, and carefully planned building upgrades rather than overwhelming the player with countless systems. Several Building upgrades require the right resources such as rice or other goods that you can obtain through either trade or capturing provinces with the resources. 

Diplomacy is where it could seem a little lacking, there's the typical alliances, trade agreements, marriages, and military but it could seem a bit unpredictable at times as some factions just don't want to deal with you despite being on the very friendly term with your clan.

The battles are where Shogun 2 truly shines. Rather than relying on flashy abilities or overpowered hero units, every battle is won through careful positioning, timing, and unit composition. The game embraces the classic rock ,paper, scissors design. Terrain plays a decisive role. Holding high ground, defending river crossings, or hiding troops in forests can completely change the outcome of a battle. Morale is the most important aspect, with disciplined formations capable of routing armies far larger than their own if their flanks are exposed or their general falls in combat. You can also beat armies with superior units with all the right strategies and positioning. Nothing's better than being badly outnumbered and despite all odds still being able to out maneuver the enemy and finally hearing "My lord a glorious victory would soon be yours!" The Unit animation re…

One of the best strategy games ever made. The atmosphere, soundtrack, and Japanese setting are outstanding, and the battles still feel satisfying even after all these years.

The game isn't perfect, though. The AI can be frustrating at times, diplomacy often feels unreliable, and the Realm Divide mechanic can make the late game feel repetitive. Despite these flaws, the core gameplay is so strong that it's easy to come back for "just one more campaign."

If you enjoy grand strategy and tactical battles, Shogun 2 is absolutely worth playing.

citations.review_text: This game is just timeless. Runs on a Potato because it came out in 2011ish

probably the most stable and reliable total war game especially since theres a workshop. fall of the samurai gives you a more than a taste of Empire in terms of fighting style warfare. fall of the samurai if like rome 2. its really nice morning sun mod needs to be something the developers for future games look into id buy it in a heart beat being a stable DLC over a potentially crappy made mod made for certain types of proccessors and computers (high value/1500-2000+dollars)

Over a dozen Total War titles have launched since Shogun 2 debuted in 2011, yet it is still one of the absolute best in the series. It captures the nostalgic, classic charm of the older games and a distinct aesthetic that none of the other games have been able to replicate. And regardless of its age, it still runs good as new. As of 2026, I still come back to it for more.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe naval warfare mechanics as problematic, noting that single-ship fleets crowd trade lanes and require tedious individual movement.

citations.review_text: First Total War game I ever played and will probably always be my favorite, even with it's older graphics I think it's the prettiest Total War game ever made I have so many screenshots from this game that almost look like paintings, the atmosphere is perfect. Big Cavalry charges on an enemies rear is still 15 years later the most satisfying thing in all of total war, you will genuinely feel love in your heart when you witness it. The passion and personality in this game is endlessly charming. If you got into the franchise with the more modern games and found the classics to be a bit too janky this is the perfect sweet spot, it still holds up to this day, yes the naval battles will make you tear your hair out, but sometimes you need suffering to fully appreciate joy. God I don't want to stop glazing this game it's so good.

Shogun 2 is one of the best of the Total Wars, but since all the dlc's are now folded into one item on Steam I'd really like to talk about Fall of the Samurai. A lot of the flaws are the same as the main game, so this is...close to being a review of that. Anyways if you're into FoTS and want a review of the latter campaign here you go.

FoTS gets the narrowest of thumbs up for me. Did you enjoy Empire Total War? Or rather, did you want to? Shogun 2: FoTS can really scratch that itch for you then. The AI's far superior, even capable of some surprises and basic strategy like seizing high ground or wide flank attacks with their cavalry. The diplomacy system functions well enough, and the unit variety is interesting and keeps you going.

The massive, massive, massive caveat to this is naval warfare. Without mods (like disabling most ship types), when the endgame triggers you should expect to find anywhere between 8-15 single ship fleets parked on your trade lanes at any given moment. You will then feel the real life minutes of your life tick by as each one moves individually to bleed your economy still further. If you don't engage in this system, in time these ships will creep in range and bombard your ports, compounding the problem further. If you do engage in this system, be prepared for an autoresolve that ensures your expensive fleet sinks one little cleanup operation at a time, or naval combat proper which requires spending minutes just closing the distance while the AI camps at the back of its own deployment zone. 

In a sentence, anything to do with the maritime game here is deeply unfun and unengaging. Land combat/sieges/naval support fire is a delight and the tech and economy balances work well. But lord knows if I'll ever finish a campaign of this.
